reviews.text: Please do NOT buy any pets from this store. I saw a tiny kitty in the window without water or any possibility to jump or to climb on very little space. It's just abuse. Why does this store even exist??? How is it possible that people see this and nothing happens?

We currently have one dog and were considering getting a second one, so we visited this store the other day.

When a staff member approached us and allowed us to hold a puppy, they asked, "Where do you live?" and we replied, "Tokyo." They then asked, "Are you from far away?" to which we replied that we are from the Kansai region.

Immediately afterward, without any explanation, they suddenly took the puppy from our arms and walked away.

We were shocked and extremely offended by their abrupt response. Do they judge whether or not to accept a dog based on its place of origin? If there is a reason, shouldn't they properly explain it?

Whether or not there was discriminatory intent is unclear, but this customer service left us with nothing but doubts and distrust. Because it's a place to welcome a precious family member, we want to choose a store where we can consider adoption with peace of mind. We will not be getting a second dog from this store.

Dogs are sold as if they were clothes in stores.
The little dogs in transparent boxes 😔 …

The staff's customer service was extremely disappointing. I wouldn't recommend going there, as you'll only have a bad experience.

While I was looking at the pets, they blocked my view to start feeding them, and then completely ignored me while only attending to other customers who arrived later. Even after those customers left, they continued playing with the pets without even glancing at me, even though I was still in the store. They didn't even offer basic compliments like "Aren't they cute?"

I was ignored while looking at merchandise, but then they gave me an overly cheerful "Thank you" as I was leaving, which was very unpleasant.

Perhaps because all the pets are quite old, the staff's quality seems low. I will never go there again.

absolutely vile these places are allowed to exist. the animals have no room to run around and have nothing to entertain them. All bred so badly to be as cute as possible with no care to their health and definitely too young to be away from their mothers. Shame on anyone who supports businesses like this.

A store that has lost all customer service. It's the same even if there's no one there. I couldn't hear anyone at all... Some employees were just playing with their cell phones. I felt sorry for the dogs and cats being sold.

„Pets always come first” even their name is a total scam. These people keep these poor animals in cages, not allowing them to go out once!! At the age of six or more months. And guess what happens when they reach an age where they are not “valuable” anymore….

I visited the Aoyama store.
As I could not find any signs prohibiting photography at the store entrance or inside the store, I took photos without using a flash, being considerate of those around me, to use as reference for considering a purchase.
When I did, a staff member told me, "Photography is prohibited in our store," but did not explain why.
Since photography was allowed at other stores, I found it difficult to understand the rules per store.
If photography was prohibited, I feel that if there had been a clear sign or explanation explaining the reason in advance, I would not have had this confusion.
I feel very disappointed.

Horrible experience here. Staff was so rude towards me when I asked if I could see the pets because someone else was playing with the pets right before me. But all she said was only people with intentions to buy could pet them. Will never recommend this place to anyone.

If you read the reviews from buyers of this store, you’ll see that health issues popped up after purchasing their pets. Do not buy your pets from this store. As others have mentioned, separating baby animals from their mothers and litters this early causes long-term health issues. This compounds with unethical breeding practices to make the dogs and cats as small and cute as possible. Being subjected to no physical contact and confinement is not healthy for any living being, especially during infancy. The clerk seems to offer no affection or compassion to the animals either. All he did was stare at them, walk around, and look at his computer. Unfriendly short man. He didn’t want us to take photo or videos, which is the first time a clerk at a P’s First has said that. We played with the kittens for a bit to give them some stimulation, but I couldn’t help but feel sadness after leaving the store.

I bought a cat at this Ebisu branch, and since it's close to my home, I go to check it out occasionally.

However, the prices are surprisingly high.

The conditions in which the animals are kept are unacceptable - too quickly taken from the mother, placed in transparent cages under constant artificial light, with no enrichment. I cried walking past this store. This whole place should be banned.
Heart breaking. If you love animals don’t go here. 🙁💔 …

The salesperson's approach was awful.
They quickly pulled out a car worth about ¥800,000
and showed it to me, but all they said was:

"Even students often buy cars straight away. They can get loans. Students tend to be braver. I even had a 20-year-old student buy one recently. On the other hand, do you think they'd buy one for that price?"
(As if I, a working adult, had no guts.)

When it came to getting a quote, they offered peace of mind support (something I didn't think was worth it and didn't need).
"We're a business, too, so it's a must for you to include it."

No, I think there are better ways to say it.
In the end, I decided not to buy one here.

This pet shop is absolutely not recommended. Beyond the fact that the animals are ridiculously expensive, they're displayed like objects in any ordinary store. They're kept in small, transparent plastic cages, often alone. Seeing that literally broke my heart.
this is unethical. shame on you when there are many dogs and cats waiting to be rescued.
The attitude of the elderly woman was terrible, which made me feel very uncomfortable, and I regretted going into the store.
